Using the tangent gradient for the normal instead of the negative reciprocal
Solving numerator = 0 for horizontal tangents but not substituting back into the curve, giving points that are not on it

threads.echo: A horizontal tangent on an implicit curve is a local highest or lowest point of that branch, found as before from dy/dx = 0.

skills.name: Find a related rate from a given formula
examTypes: The radius of a sphere increases at 0.3 cm s⁻¹. Find the rate of increase of its volume when r = 5 cm
The area of a square decreases at 4 cm² s⁻¹. Find the rate at which its side changes when the side is 10 cm
Find dθ/dt when x = 3, given that tan θ = x/4 and dx/dt = 2

methods.name: Chain rule product
methods.summary: Write the wanted rate as a product of known derivatives, e.g. dV/dt = dV/dr × dr/dt = 4πr² × 0.3 = 30π at r = 5.

methods.name: Differentiate the relation with respect to t
methods.summary: Differentiate both sides of the formula implicitly with respect to time, then substitute the known values.

misconceptions: Substituting r = 5 into V before differentiating, so V is constant and dV/dt = 0
Inverting a factor: using dr/dV instead of dV/dr
Ignoring the sign of a decreasing quantity, giving +0.2 cm s⁻¹ instead of −0.2 cm s⁻¹ for the square's side

threads.echo: Rates chain together like exchange rates: cm³ per cm times cm per second gives cm³ per second.

skills.name: Set up and solve a related-rates problem from a description
examTypes: A 5 m ladder slides down a wall with its foot moving away at 0.5 m s⁻¹. How fast is the top moving when the foot is 3 m from the wall?
Water flows into an inverted cone of height 12 cm and radius 4 cm at 2 cm³ s⁻¹. Find the rate the depth rises when it is 6 cm
A plane flies at constant height past an observer. Find the rate of change of the angle of elevation at a given moment

methods.name: Find a relation, then differentiate in t
methods.summary: Write an equation linking the variables (Pythagoras, similar triangles, trigonometry), differentiate with respect to t and substitute: for the ladder 2x x′ + 2y y′ = 0 gives y′ = −3 × 0.5/4 = −0.375 m s⁻¹.

methods.name: Eliminate with similar triangles
methods.summary: Use the fixed shape to remove a variable first, e.g. r = h/3 in the cone so V = πh³/27, then use the chain rule.

misconceptions: Substituting the instantaneous values (x = 3, y = 4) before differentiating
Keeping both r and h in the cone formula and treating r as constant, giving dV/dh = πr²/3
Treating the rate of the top of the ladder as positive, though it moves down

threads.echo: A fixed relationship between two quantities fixes how their rates are linked: if x² + y² stays 25, x growing forces y to shrink.

skills.name: Solve optimisation problems, including when the optimum is at an endpoint
examTypes: A swimmer can swim at 2 m s⁻¹ and run at 5 m s⁻¹. Find where she should land to reach the point in the least time
Find the maximum value of the area for 0 ≤ θ ≤ π/2 and justify that it is a maximum
Show that the stationary point does not give the least cost, and find the least cost on the given domain

methods.name: Compare stationary values with endpoints
methods.summary: Form the one-variable function on its feasible domain, find stationary points, then evaluate the function at those and at both ends and choose the best.

methods.name: Graph over the feasible domain
methods.summary: Graph the model only over the values that make sense and read the maximum or minimum, including at the ends.

methods.name: Monotonic means endpoint
methods.summary: If the derivative keeps one sign on the domain (or the stationary point lies outside it), the optimum must be at an endpoint.

misconceptions: Taking the stationary point as the answer when it lies outside the feasible domain
Assuming a stationary point is the minimum when it is a maximum, and not checking the endpoints
Writing the time as total distance over average speed instead of adding the two separate times

threads.echo: On a closed domain the extreme value can sit at an end, just as a parabola restricted to one side of its vertex has its maximum at the edge.

subtopics.title: Further standard derivatives and integrals
subtopics.guide: Derivatives of tan x, sec x, cosec x, cot x, aˣ, logₐ x, arcsin x, arccos x and arctan x, the matching indefinite integrals (read as a family of curves), and the same results for composites with a linear function. Partial fractions (up to two distinct linear factors) are used to rearrange integrands.

skills.name: Differentiate tan, sec, cosec and cot, including composites
examTypes: Find f′(x) for f(x) = sec 3x
Differentiate x² cot x
Find the gradient of y = cosec(2x + 1) at x = 0

methods.name: Standard derivatives with the chain rule
methods.summary: Use d/dx tan x = sec² x, sec x → sec x tan x, cosec x → −cosec x cot x, cot x → −cosec² x, and multiply by the derivative of the inside.

methods.name: Rewrite as a power of sin or cos
methods.summary: Write sec x = (cos x)⁻¹ and use the chain rule: −(cos x)⁻² × (−sin x) = sec x tan x.

methods.name: Quotient rule
methods.summary: Treat tan x = sin x/cos x or cot x = cos x/sin x as a quotient and simplify with sin² x + cos² x = 1.

misconceptions: Dropping the minus for the co-functions: d/dx cot x = cosec² x
Forgetting the chain-rule factor: d/dx sec 3x = sec 3x tan 3x
Writing d/dx tan x = sec x

threads.echo: Swapping each function for its co-function (tan ↔ cot, sec ↔ cosec) turns one derivative into the other with a minus sign, because cos x = sin(π/2 − x).

skills.name: Differentiate aˣ and logₐ x
examTypes: Find dy/dx for y = 5ˣ
Differentiate log₃(2x + 1)
Find the gradient of y = 2^(x²) at x = 1

methods.name: Standard results
methods.summary: Use d/dx aˣ = aˣ ln a and d/dx logₐ x = 1/(x ln a), with the chain rule for composites.

methods.name: Rewrite with base e
methods.summary: Write aˣ = e^(x ln a) or logₐ x = ln x/ln a and differentiate the familiar base-e forms.

misconceptions: Using the power rule on an exponential: d/dx 5ˣ = x·5^(x−1)
Writing d/dx 5ˣ = 5ˣ, forgetting the factor ln 5
Putting ln a in the numerator: d/dx logₐ x = (ln a)/x

threads.echo: Every exponential aˣ grows at a rate proportional to itself; ln a is the constant of proportionality, and it is 1 exactly when a = e.

skills.name: Differentiate arcsin, arccos and arctan, including composites
examTypes: Find dy/dx for y = arctan 2x
Differentiate arcsin(x/3)
Show that d/dx (arcsin x + arccos x) = 0 and interpret the result

methods.name: Standard results with the chain rule
methods.summary: Use 1/√(1 − x²), −1/√(1 − x²) and 1/(1 + x²), then multiply by the derivative of the inside: arctan 2x → 2/(1 + 4x²).

methods.name: Derive implicitly
methods.summary: Write y = arctan x as tan y = x, differentiate: sec² y dy/dx = 1, so dy/dx = 1/(1 + tan² y) = 1/(1 + x²).

misconceptions: Not squaring the whole inside: d/dx arctan 2x = 2/(1 + 2x²)
Confusing arcsin x with 1/sin x and differentiating it as −cos x/sin² x
Missing the minus sign for arccos x

threads.echo: The derivative of an inverse function is the reciprocal of the original's derivative, read at the matching point: dy/dx = 1/(dx/dy).

skills.name: Integrate the new standard forms, including linear composites
examTypes: Find ∫ sec²(3x − 1) dx
Find ∫ 1/(9 + x²) dx
Find ∫ 4ˣ dx
Find the equation of the curve through (0, 2) whose gradient is 1/√(1 − x²)

methods.name: Read a derivative backwards
methods.summary: Use the booklet: ∫ 1/(a² + x²) dx = (1/a) arctan(x/a) + C, ∫ 1/√(a² − x²) dx = arcsin(x/a) + C, ∫ aˣ dx = aˣ/ln a + C, and divide by the coefficient of x for a linear inside.

methods.name: Substitute u = ax + b
methods.summary: Let u = 3x − 1, so dx = du/3, integrate in u and substitute back.

methods.name: Differentiate to check
methods.summary: Differentiate the answer; it should give exactly the integrand.

misconceptions: Forgetting the 1/a: ∫ 1/(9 + x²) dx = arctan(x/3) + C
Writing ∫ 4ˣ dx = 4ˣ⁺¹/(x + 1) + C by the power rule
Treating the + C as optional, so the whole family of curves collapses to one

threads.echo: Every new integral is a new derivative read backwards: d/dx arctan x = 1/(1 + x²), so ∫ 1/(1 + x²) dx = arctan x + C.
The answers form a family of curves, each a vertical translation of the others; one given point picks out one curve.

skills.name: Complete the square to reach an arctan or arcsin integral
examTypes: Find ∫ 1/(x² + 6x + 13) dx
Write 8 + 2x − x² in the form a² − (x − b)², and hence find ∫ 1/√(8 + 2x − x²) dx
Evaluate ∫ from 1 to 3 of 1/(x² − 2x + 5) dx exactly

methods.name: Complete the square, then use the standard form
methods.summary: x² + 6x + 13 = (x + 3)² + 4, so the integral is ½ arctan((x + 3)/2) + C; similarly 8 + 2x − x² = 9 − (x − 1)² gives arcsin((x − 1)/3) + C.

methods.name: Substitute u = x + p
methods.summary: Let u = x + 3 to turn the integrand into 1/(u² + 4), integrate, then shift back.

misconceptions: Forgetting the ½ and giving arctan((x + 3)/2) + C
Choosing arcsin for 1/((x + 3)² + 4), which has no square root
Completing the square with a sign error: x² + 6x + 13 = (x + 3)² + 22

threads.echo: Completing the square shows the integrand is 1/(x² + 4) translated 3 units left, so the answer is the arctan graph translated in the same way.
Rewriting the quadratic in completed-square form exposes the a² + u² shape that the standard integral needs.

skills.name: Integrate using partial fractions
examTypes: Express (5x + 1)/((x − 1)(x + 2)) in partial fractions and hence find its integral
Find ∫ 3/(x² − x − 2) dx
Show that ∫ from 2 to 4 of 1/(x(x − 1)) dx = ln(3/2)

methods.name: Substitute the roots to find A and B
methods.summary: From 5x + 1 = A(x + 2) + B(x − 1), put x = 1 to get A = 2 and x = −2 to get B = 3, so the integral is 2 ln|x − 1| + 3 ln|x + 2| + C.

methods.name: Compare coefficients
methods.summary: Expand the identity and equate coefficients of x and the constants, then solve the pair of equations.

methods.name: Combine with log laws
methods.summary: After integrating, use log laws to write the answer as a single logarithm, e.g. ln|(x − 1)/x| + C, which is useful for exact definite values.

misconceptions: Writing the integral as ln|(x − 1)(x + 2)| + C, ignoring the coefficients A and B
Missing the ½ when a factor is 2x + 1: ∫ 1/(2x + 1) dx = ln|2x + 1| + C
Trying arctan on a denominator that factorises into distinct linear factors

threads.echo: The single fraction and its partial fractions are the same function; only the split form matches the standard result ∫ 1/(x − a) dx = ln|x − a| + C.

subtopics.title: Integration by substitution and by parts
subtopics.guide: Integration by substitution beyond the reverse chain rule (the substitution is given unless the integral has the form ∫ k g′(x) f(g(x)) dx), with changed limits for definite integrals. Integration by parts, including repeated use and the cyclic case such as ∫ eˣ sin x dx.

skills.name: Integrate using a given substitution
examTypes: Use the substitution u = x + 1 to find ∫ x√(x + 1) dx
Using u = √x, find ∫ 1/(1 + √x) dx
Use u = eˣ to find ∫ eˣ/(e^(2x) + 1) dx

methods.name: Replace every x and dx
methods.summary: Write x and dx in terms of u (for u = √x, x = u² and dx = 2u du), simplify to a standard integral in u, integrate and substitute back.

methods.name: Differentiate the answer
methods.summary: Differentiate the final expression in x to confirm it gives the original integrand.

misconceptions: Replacing dx by du without the factor, e.g. dx = du instead of 2u du for u = √x
Leaving some x terms in the u-integral, such as ∫ x√u du
Forgetting to substitute back, leaving the answer in terms of u

threads.echo: Substitution is the chain rule run backwards: choosing u undoes the inner function that the chain rule built.

skills.name: Evaluate a definite integral by substitution, changing the limits
examTypes: Using x = sin θ, show that ∫ from 0 to 1 of √(1 − x²) dx = π/4
Use u = x + 1 to evaluate ∫ from 0 to 3 of x√(x + 1) dx exactly
Use u = ln x to find ∫ from e to e² of 1/(x ln x) dx

methods.name: Convert the limits to u
methods.summary: Change the x-limits to u-limits as you substitute and finish in u: for u = x + 1 the limits 0 and 3 become 1 and 4, giving 116/15.

methods.name: Substitute back, keep x-limits
methods.summary: Find the antiderivative in x first, then use the original limits; longer but equally valid.

methods.name: Check numerically
methods.summary: Evaluate the original definite integral on the GDC to confirm the exact value (on Paper 2).

misconceptions: Using the old x-limits with the u-antiderivative
Converting limits for x = sin θ as θ = 0 to 1 instead of 0 to π/2
Dropping the dx = cos θ dθ factor, which gives ∫ cos θ dθ = 1 instead of π/4

threads.echo: Substitution relabels the strips under the curve; the total area stays the same as long as the limits move with the new variable.

skills.name: Integrate a product by parts once
examTypes: Find ∫ x cos x dx
Find ∫ x e^(2x) dx
Find ∫ x² ln x dx

methods.name: ∫ u dv = uv − ∫ v du
methods.summary: Choose u to be the factor that simplifies when differentiated (usually the power of x, but ln x when present), integrate the other factor, and apply the formula.

methods.name: Tabular (DI) layout
methods.summary: List successive derivatives of u and integrals of dv in two columns and combine diagonally with alternating signs.

methods.name: Differentiate the answer
methods.summary: Use the product rule on the result to recover the integrand.

misconceptions: Sign error: ∫ x cos x dx = x sin x − cos x + C instead of x sin x + cos x + C
Choosing u = e^(2x) and dv = x dx, which leads to the harder integral ∫ x² e^(2x) dx
Missing a factor: ∫ x e^(2x) dx = ½x e^(2x) − ½e^(2x) + C instead of ½x e^(2x) − ¼e^(2x) + C

threads.echo: Integration by parts is the product rule read backwards: (uv)′ = u′v + uv′ rearranged and integrated.

skills.name: Integrate ln x, arctan x or arcsin x by parts with dv = 1
examTypes: Find ∫ ln x dx
Find ∫ arctan x dx
Evaluate ∫ from 0 to ½ of arcsin x dx

methods.name: Write as 1 × f(x)
methods.summary: Take u = f(x) and dv = 1, so ∫ arctan x dx = x arctan x − ∫ x/(1 + x²) dx = x arctan x − ½ ln(1 + x²) + C.

methods.name: Use a given derivative
methods.summary: If told d/dx (x ln x) = ln x + 1, integrate both sides and rearrange to get ∫ ln x dx = x ln x − x + C.

misconceptions: Writing ∫ ln x dx = 1/x + C, confusing integration with differentiation
Stopping at x ln x and missing the − x
Integrating x/(1 + x²) as ln(1 + x²) without the ½

threads.echo: The integrals of the inverse functions ln, arcsin and arctan come from their derivatives, which are algebraic, so parts swaps a hard integrand for an easy one.

skills.name: Use repeated integration by parts, including the cyclic case
examTypes: Find ∫ x² eˣ dx
Find ∫ eˣ sin x dx
Find ∫ e^(2x) cos x dx

methods.name: Apply parts twice
methods.summary: Reduce the power of x by one each time: ∫ x² eˣ dx = eˣ(x² − 2x + 2) + C.

methods.name: Call the integral I and solve
methods.summary: For eˣ sin x, apply parts twice with the same type of choice; the original integral reappears, so 2I = eˣ(sin x − cos x) and I = ½eˣ(sin x − cos x) + C.

methods.name: Tabular (DI) layout
methods.summary: List derivatives of x² down to 0 beside repeated integrals of eˣ and combine with alternating signs.

misconceptions: Swapping the choice of u on the second application in the cyclic case, which only gives I = I
Sign slip in the second step: eˣ(x² − 2x − 2) + C
Forgetting to divide by 2 after collecting I, giving eˣ(sin x − cos x) + C

threads.echo: In the cyclic case the integral is rewritten until it reappears; treating I as an unknown turns calculus into solving a linear equation.

skills.name: Choose an integration technique for an unfamiliar integral
examTypes: For each integral, state whether inspection, substitution, parts or partial fractions is most efficient
Find ∫ x/(x² + 4) dx and ∫ 1/(x² + 4) dx and explain why the methods differ
Find ∫ x³ e^(x²) dx

methods.name: Spot g′(x) beside g(x)
methods.summary: If a multiple of an inner function's derivative is present, use inspection or substitution: x/(x² + 4) gives ½ ln(x² + 4) + C.

methods.name: Rearrange the integrand
methods.summary: Partial fractions for factorising denominators, completing the square for irreducible quadratics (1/(x² + 4) gives ½ arctan(x/2) + C).

methods.name: Parts for unrelated products
methods.summary: Use parts when the factors are unrelated (power times exponential, trig or log); ∫ x³ e^(x²) dx needs u = x², then parts in u.

misconceptions: Missing the ½ when x is half the derivative of x² + 4: ∫ x/(x² + 4) dx = ln(x² + 4) + C
Giving ln(x² + 4) for ∫ 1/(x² + 4) dx
Splitting 1/(x² + 4) into partial fractions as if it factorised

threads.echo: Choosing a technique is choosing which equivalent form of the integrand to work with: split, substituted or written as a product.

subtopics.title: Areas against the y-axis and volumes of revolution
subtopics.guide: Areas between a curve and the y-axis over a y-interval, found by integrating x with respect to y. Volumes of solids formed by rotating a region through 2π about the x-axis (V = π∫ y² dx) or the y-axis (V = π∫ x² dy), including regions between two curves and design contexts.

skills.name: Find the area between a curve and the y-axis
examTypes: Find the area enclosed by y = x², the y-axis and the line y = 4, for x ≥ 0
Find the area between x = y² − 4y and the y-axis
Find the area of the region bounded by y = ln x, the y-axis, y = 0 and y = 2

methods.name: Integrate x with respect to y
methods.summary: Rearrange to x = g(y) and find ∫ |g(y)| dy between the y-limits: ∫₀⁴ √y dy = 16/3.

methods.name: Rectangle minus the x-area
methods.summary: Subtract the area under the curve (against the x-axis) from a bounding rectangle: 2 × 4 − ∫₀² x² dx = 8 − 8/3 = 16/3.

methods.name: GDC with y as the variable
methods.summary: On Paper 2, enter g(y) as a function and evaluate the definite integral numerically, using the absolute value if part lies left of the axis.

misconceptions: Using the y-limits with the x-integrand: ∫₀⁴ x² dx = 64/3
Not rearranging, so the integrand is still in terms of x
Giving a negative area when the region lies to the left of the y-axis (e.g. −32/3 for x = y² − 4y)

threads.echo: The same adding-up of thin strips works sideways: horizontal strips of width x and thickness δy add up to ∫ x dy.
Integrating x = √y against y gives the same region as the inverse function y = x² viewed from the other axis.

skills.name: Find a volume of revolution about the x-axis
examTypes: The region under y = √x from x = 0 to x = 4 is rotated through 2π about the x-axis. Find the volume
Find the exact volume formed when y = sec x, 0 ≤ x ≤ π/4, is rotated about the x-axis
Show that rotating y = (r/h)x for 0 ≤ x ≤ h gives the volume of a cone, (1/3)πr²h

methods.name: Discs: V = π∫ y² dx
methods.summary: Square y, integrate between the x-limits and multiply by π: π∫₀⁴ x dx = 8π.

methods.name: GDC integral
methods.summary: On Paper 2, evaluate π∫ (f(x))² dx numerically.

methods.name: Check with a known solid
methods.summary: Where the solid is a cone, cylinder or sphere, compare with its standard volume formula.

misconceptions: Forgetting π, giving 8 instead of 8π
Not squaring y: π∫₀⁴ √x dx = 16π/3
Squaring the integral instead of the function: π(∫₀⁴ √x dx)² = 256π/9

threads.echo: The solid is a stack of thin discs, each of volume πy² δx, and the integral adds them up.

skills.name: Find a volume of revolution about the y-axis
examTypes: The region between y = x², the y-axis and y = 4 is rotated through 2π about the y-axis. Find the volume
Find the volume of the bowl formed by rotating y = ln x, 0 ≤ y ≤ 2, about the y-axis
A curve is given as y = f(x). Write down an integral for its volume about the y-axis in terms of y

methods.name: Discs: V = π∫ x² dy
methods.summary: Rearrange for x² in terms of y, integrate between the y-limits and multiply by π: π∫₀⁴ y dy = 8π.

methods.name: GDC with y as variable
methods.summary: On Paper 2, enter x² as a function of y and evaluate π times its integral numerically.

misconceptions: Keeping the x-limits: π∫₀² y dy = 2π instead of 8π
Using π∫ y² dx, which rotates about the wrong axis (π∫₀² x⁴ dx = 32π/5)
Rearranging wrongly, e.g. x² = eʸ for y = ln x instead of x² = e^(2y)

threads.echo: Now the discs are horizontal, each of volume πx² δy, stacked up the y-axis.

skills.name: Find the volume when a region between two curves is rotated
examTypes: The region between y = x and y = x² is rotated through 2π about the x-axis. Find the volume
Find the volume when the region between y = 4 − x² and y = 3 is rotated about the x-axis
Find the volume when the region between two curves is rotated about the y-axis

methods.name: Washers: outer² − inner²
methods.summary: Find the intersections, then V = π∫ (y_outer² − y_inner²) dx: π∫₀¹ (x² − x⁴) dx = 2π/15.

methods.name: Subtract two solids
methods.summary: Find the volume from the outer curve and subtract the volume from the inner curve over the same limits.

methods.name: GDC intersections and integral
methods.summary: On Paper 2, find the intersections with the GDC and evaluate π∫ (f² − g²) dx numerically.

misconceptions: Squaring the difference: π∫₀¹ (x − x²)² dx = π/30 instead of 2π/15
Putting the inner curve first, giving a negative volume
Using wrong limits because the intersections were not found first

threads.echo: Each slice is a washer, a disc with a hole, so its volume is π(R² − r²) δx and the integral adds the washers.
The limits are the intersections of the two curves, found by algebra when possible and by GDC when not.

skills.name: Model a designed object as a solid of revolution
examTypes: A vase is modelled by rotating a given curve about the y-axis. Find its capacity
Find the depth of liquid in the bowl when it holds 500 cm³
Show that rotating x² + y² = r² gives the volume of a sphere, (4/3)πr³

methods.name: Set up the integral and evaluate
methods.summary: Pick the axis of rotation, write the radius squared in terms of the integration variable and integrate between the given limits.

methods.name: Solve for an unknown limit
methods.summary: Write the volume as a function of the upper limit h, then solve V(h) = given value on the GDC.

methods.name: Use symmetry
methods.summary: For a sphere or other symmetric profile, integrate from 0 to r and double.

misconceptions: Rotating about the wrong axis for the shape described (a vase standing upright needs the y-axis)
Mixing units, e.g. using cm for the profile but litres for the capacity
Solving for the volume when the depth is asked for

threads.echo: Any solid with circular cross-sections is a sum of discs; the formula for a cone or a sphere is just one such sum.

subtopics.title: First-order differential equations
subtopics.guide: First-order differential equations: numerical solution of dy/dx = f(x, y) by Euler's method with constant step h; exact solution of separable equations (including the logistic equation, using partial fractions), homogeneous equations dy/dx = f(y/x) via y = vx, and linear equations y′ + P(x)y = Q(x) via an integrating factor. Contexts include cooling, population growth and radioactive decay.

skills.name: Approximate a solution with Euler's method
examTypes: Use Euler's method with h = 0.1 to estimate y(0.3) for dy/dx = x + y, y(0) = 1
Explain whether the Euler estimate is an overestimate or an underestimate
State how the accuracy of the approximation could be improved

methods.name: Step by hand
methods.summary: Use yₙ₊₁ = yₙ + h f(xₙ, yₙ) and xₙ₊₁ = xₙ + h: from (0, 1), y₁ = 1.1, y₂ = 1.1 + 0.1(1.2) = 1.22.

methods.name: GDC sequence or spreadsheet
methods.summary: Enter the recurrence in the sequence mode or a spreadsheet and read off the required term.

methods.name: Follow tangent lines
methods.summary: Each step moves along the tangent at the current point; if the true curve is concave up, the estimates fall below it.

misconceptions: Using the new x with the old y, f(xₙ₊₁, yₙ), for the gradient
Forgetting to multiply the gradient by h, so y₁ = 1 + 1 = 2
Taking the wrong number of steps, e.g. two steps to reach x = 0.3 with h = 0.1

threads.echo: Each Euler step is the move by the vector (h, h f(x, y)): across by h, up by the gradient times h.
When an equation cannot be solved exactly, a numerical method gives the answer, and an exact solution, when there is one, checks it.

skills.name: Solve a separable differential equation
examTypes: Solve dy/dx = xy given y = 2 when x = 0
Find the general solution of dy/dx = (1 + y²) cos x
Solve dy/dx = e^(x − y), giving y in terms of x

methods.name: Separate the variables and integrate
methods.summary: Write ∫ 1/g(y) dy = ∫ f(x) dx, integrate with one constant, then use the condition: ln|y| = x²/2 + C gives y = 2e^(x²/2).

methods.name: Substitute back to verify
methods.summary: Differentiate the proposed solution and check it satisfies both the equation and the initial condition.

misconceptions: Exponentiating term by term: ln y = x²/2 + C becomes y = e^(x²/2) + C
Dropping the constant of integration, giving y = e^(x²/2), which does not satisfy y(0) = 2
Not separating fully, e.g. integrating e^(x − y) dx with y treated as a constant

threads.echo: Solving a differential equation undoes differentiation, and the constant picks one curve from the family.

skills.name: Solve the logistic equation and other separable models using partial fractions
examTypes: Solve dn/dt = 0.2n(50 − n), n(0) = 5, and find the limiting population
Show that 1/(n(a − n)) = (1/a)(1/n + 1/(a − n)) and hence solve the logistic equation
Find the time at which the population reaches half its limiting value

methods.name: Separate, split into partial fractions, integrate
methods.summary: ∫ 1/(n(a − n)) dn = (1/a) ln|n/(a − n)| = kt + C, then rearrange to n = a/(1 + Be^(−akt)).

methods.name: Read the limit from the equation
methods.summary: Setting dn/dt = 0 gives the equilibria n = 0 and n = a; the population tends to a, without solving.

methods.name: GDC for the time
methods.summary: Graph the solution and find when it reaches a given value.

misconceptions: Missing the 1/a: 1/(n(a − n)) = 1/n + 1/(a − n)
Integrating 1/(a − n) as +ln|a − n| instead of −ln|a − n|
Giving the initial value or the rate k as the limiting value instead of a

threads.echo: For small n the logistic model is almost dn/dt = kan, pure exponential growth; the factor (a − n) brakes it toward the ceiling a.

skills.name: Form and interpret a differential equation in context
examTypes: A drink cools at a rate proportional to the difference between its temperature and the room's 20 °C. Write a differential equation and solve it
Carbon-14 decays at a rate proportional to the amount present. Given the half-life, find the age of a sample
Interpret the sign of k in dP/dt = kP in context

methods.name: Translate 'proportional to' into an equation
methods.summary: Write the rate as k times the stated quantity, e.g. dT/dt = −k(T − 20), with the sign chosen from the context.

methods.name: Solve, then fit constants
methods.summary: Separate to get T = 20 + Ae^(−kt), use two data points to find A and k, then answer the question.

methods.name: Solve for the unknown on the GDC
methods.summary: Once the model is found, use the GDC to solve for a time or value.

misconceptions: Writing dT/dt = −kT, which makes the drink cool to 0 °C instead of room temperature
Choosing the wrong sign, so a cooling object heats up
Using the half-life as the decay constant instead of k = ln 2 / half-life

threads.echo: A rate proportional to the amount present gives exponential change: decay, growth and cooling are repeated multiplication in continuous time.
Newton's cooling solution 20 + Ae^(−kt) is plain exponential decay translated up by the room temperature.

skills.name: Solve a homogeneous differential equation with y = vx
examTypes: Use y = vx to solve dy/dx = (x + y)/x
Show that the substitution y = vx turns dy/dx = (x² + y²)/(xy) into a separable equation
Solve dy/dx = (y² + 2xy)/x² given y = 1 when x = 1

methods.name: Substitute y = vx
methods.summary: Use dy/dx = v + x dv/dx, simplify to a separable equation in v and x, solve, then replace v by y/x: dy/dx = 1 + y/x gives y = x ln|x| + Cx.

methods.name: Verify by substitution
methods.summary: Differentiate the solution and substitute into the original equation to check.

misconceptions: Writing dy/dx = v (or dv/dx), forgetting the product rule on vx
Forgetting to replace v by y/x at the end
Applying y = vx to an equation that is not a function of y/x

threads.echo: Rewriting the equation in terms of v = y/x does not change it, but in the new form the variables separate.

skills.name: Solve a linear equation y′ + P(x)y = Q(x) with an integrating factor
examTypes: Solve dy/dx + 2y = eˣ
Solve x dy/dx + y = x³ for x > 0, given y(1) = 1
Find the integrating factor for dy/dx + y tan x = cos x

methods.name: Multiply by e^(∫P dx)
methods.summary: Put the equation in standard form, multiply by I = e^(∫P dx) so the left side is (Iy)′, integrate and divide by I: dy/dx + 2y = eˣ gives y = eˣ/3 + Ce^(−2x).

methods.name: Spot an exact product
methods.summary: Sometimes the left side is already a product derivative: x y′ + y = (xy)′, so xy = x⁴/4 + C directly.

misconceptions: Using e^(P(x)) instead of e^(∫P dx), e.g. e^(2) for P = 2
Not dividing by the coefficient of y′ first: for x y′ + 2y = x³, using e^(2x) instead of x²
Dividing only part of the right side by the integrating factor: y = eˣ/3 + C instead of eˣ/3 + Ce^(−2x)

threads.echo: The integrating factor rewrites y′ + Py as the derivative of a single product, (Iy)′, which can be integrated at once.

subtopics.title: Maclaurin series
subtopics.guide: Maclaurin series for eˣ, sin x, cos x, ln(1 + x) and (1 + x)ᵖ with p rational, and new series built from these by substitution, multiplication, differentiation and integration. Series can also be developed from a differential equation by repeated differentiation.

skills.name: Derive a Maclaurin series from derivatives at 0
examTypes: Find the first three non-zero terms of the Maclaurin series for sec x
Show that the Maclaurin series of ln(1 + x) begins x − x²/2 + x³/3
Find the Maclaurin series of e^(sin x) up to the x² term

methods.name: f(0) + x f′(0) + x²f″(0)/2! + …
methods.summary: Differentiate repeatedly, evaluate each derivative at 0, and divide the nth one by n!: for sec x, f(0) = 1, f′(0) = 0, f″(0) = 1, so sec x ≈ 1 + x²/2.

methods.name: Build from known series
methods.summary: Where possible, combine standard series instead, e.g. e^(sin x) ≈ 1 + sin x + sin² x/2 ≈ 1 + x + x²/2.

misconceptions: Leaving out the factorials, so the x² coefficient is f″(0) instead of f″(0)/2
Writing derivatives evaluated at x instead of 0 into the series
Stopping at three terms of the series when three non-zero terms are asked for

threads.echo: A Maclaurin series stores a function as its value, slope, rate of change of slope and so on at x = 0.

skills.name: Use the standard series and the binomial series (1 + x)ᵖ
examTypes: Write down the first three terms of the series for √(1 + x)
Use the series for ln(1 + x) to estimate ln 1.1
Find the series for 1/(1 − 2x)² up to x³ and state its interval of validity

methods.name: Formula booklet series
methods.summary: Use the listed series; (1 + x)ᵖ = 1 + px + p(p − 1)x²/2! + …, so √(1 + x) ≈ 1 + x/2 − x²/8.

methods.name: Derive from derivatives
methods.summary: Rebuild the series from f(0), f′(0), f″(0) to check a coefficient.

methods.name: Compare with the GDC value
methods.summary: Evaluate the truncated series and the function at a small x to see how close they are.

misconceptions: Using factorials in the ln series: x − x²/2! + x³/3! instead of x − x²/2 + x³/3
Getting the x² coefficient of √(1 + x) as +1/8 instead of −1/8
Thinking (1 + x)ᵖ with p ∉ ℕ is valid for every x, not just |x| < 1

threads.echo: For whole-number p the series stops and gives the binomial expansion; for other rational p the same pattern carries on forever.
sin x has only odd powers and cos x only even powers, matching sin being an odd function and cos an even one.

skills.name: Obtain a new series by substitution
examTypes: Use the series for eˣ to find the series for e^(−x²) up to x⁶
Find the series for cos 2x up to x⁴
Find the series for ln(1 − 3x) and state the values of x for which it is valid

methods.name: Replace x by the new expression
methods.summary: Substitute, keeping brackets, and expand each power: cos 2x = 1 − (2x)²/2 + (2x)⁴/24 = 1 − 2x² + (2/3)x⁴.

methods.name: Derive directly
methods.summary: Differentiate the new function and evaluate at 0; slower, but a check on a coefficient.

misconceptions: Not raising the coefficient: (2x)² written as 2x², giving cos 2x = 1 − x² + …
Losing signs: e^(−x²) = 1 + x² + x⁴/2 instead of 1 − x² + x⁴/2
Keeping the original interval of validity after substituting 3x, instead of |x| < 1/3

threads.echo: Replacing x by 2x is a horizontal stretch by factor ½; in the series it multiplies the xⁿ coefficient by 2ⁿ.

skills.name: Obtain a series for a product of functions
examTypes: Find the series for eˣ sin x up to the x³ term
Find the first three non-zero terms of the series for (1 + x) ln(1 + x)
Find the series for eˣ cos x up to x³ and hence estimate a value

methods.name: Multiply and collect up to the required power
methods.summary: Take enough terms of each series, multiply out and keep only terms up to the target power: (1 + x + x²/2 + x³/6)(x − x³/6) = x + x² + x³/3 + …

methods.name: Check one coefficient from derivatives
methods.summary: Find f‴(0) for the product to confirm the x³ coefficient.

misconceptions: Using too few terms: sin x ≈ x gives eˣ sin x ≈ x + x² + x³/2, with x³ coefficient 1/2 instead of 1/3
Multiplying only matching terms, e.g. 1 × x + x × 0 + …
Keeping terms beyond the stated power with incomplete coefficients

threads.echo: Multiplying two series is multiplying two polynomials; the product is the same function written as one power series.

skills.name: Obtain a series by differentiating or integrating a known series
examTypes: By integrating the series for 1/(1 + x²), find the Maclaurin series for arctan x
Differentiate the series for ln(1 + x) to obtain the series for 1/(1 + x)
Use a series to estimate ∫ from 0 to 0.5 of e^(−x²) dx

methods.name: Term by term
methods.summary: Differentiate or integrate each term: ∫ (1 − x² + x⁴ − …) dx = x − x³/3 + x⁵/5 − … + C, with C = arctan 0 = 0.

methods.name: Compare with the GDC
methods.summary: Evaluate the definite integral on the GDC to judge the accuracy of the series estimate.

misconceptions: Leaving out the constant of integration, or not checking it is zero
Integrating xⁿ as xⁿ⁺¹ without dividing by n + 1
Using the series outside its interval of validity, e.g. for arctan 2

threads.echo: Integrating the series of a derivative undoes the differentiation and gives the series of the original function.
Integrating a series adds up the area under each simple term, giving an estimate where no exact antiderivative exists.

skills.name: Find a Maclaurin series from a differential equation
examTypes: Given dy/dx = x + y² and y(0) = 1, find the series for y up to x³
Show that y = eˣ satisfies y″ − y = 0 and use the equation to rebuild its series
Given y″ + xy = 0, y(0) = 1 and y′(0) = 0, find the first three non-zero terms

methods.name: Differentiate the equation repeatedly
methods.summary: Use the equation for y′(0), differentiate it (implicitly) for y″, then y‴: y′ = x + y² gives y′(0) = 1, y″ = 1 + 2yy′ gives 3, y‴ = 2y′² + 2yy″ gives 8, so y ≈ 1 + x + (3/2)x² + (4/3)x³.

methods.name: Substitute a power series
methods.summary: Write y = a₀ + a₁x + a₂x² + … , substitute into the equation and match coefficients of each power of x.

misconceptions: Differentiating y² as 2y instead of 2y dy/dx
Dividing by n instead of n!, giving 8x³/3 instead of 4x³/3
Using the value of y″(0) as the x² coefficient without halving it

threads.echo: The differential equation gives the rate of change at the start, and differentiating it gives the rate of change of that rate, one series term at a time.
